title: Chatter and the narrator (sessions 2 and 3 of the roadmap, done together)
claude_session: the same background job that built session 1
started_from: Emerson: "make the rest of the full crew jan thing"
intended: Give the crew voices: the 0.8B chatter lane with the quality guard the plan demands, then the 4B narrator for the day's event and the time-skip summary.

the_two_open_questions_the_plan_left.does_qwen3.5_thinking_need_turning_off: Yes, and it is not optional. Measured on the 0.8B: a plain request for one line of dialogue spent all 160 tokens in reasoning_content and returned EMPTY content in 5.7 s. The same request with chat_template_kwargs {enable_thinking: false} returned the line in 0.9 s. janclient.py sends that flag on every request and there is a test pinning it.
the_two_open_questions_the_plan_left.what_the_models_actually_cost: 0.8B chatter: 0.6-0.9 s a line, so a three-line conversation is about 3 s. 4B narrator: 21 s for 74 tokens on an empty machine, 34 s with both models loaded and a longer prompt. That gap is why the narrator runs once a station day and never where a request is waiting.

did: janhollow/janclient.py — the only way to Jan: thinking off on every call, ONE lane so two requests can never run at once (two concurrent calls once froze this laptop), a lane wait so the chatter skips its turn rather than queueing behind the narrator, and per-call stats.

janhollow/roles.py — which model each role wants and why, as a registry. This exists because of a bug found in live testing: with no setting, forge_jan falls back to whatever Jan lists FIRST, which was an unrelated 2B that leaked thinking into the crew's mouths. Precedence is now: the person's setting, then this preference, then Jan's first model.

janhollow/guard.py — the quality guard. Ten named rules in a registry, every one a pure function, every one traceable to real bad output from the 0.8B. It also salvages the line from a reply truncated mid-JSON, which is what a token limit does.

janhollow/chatter.py — picks two crew who are in the same room, standing still and not already talking; builds the prompt from persona, job, room, activity, relationship warmth and their last memory; runs two or three turns; retries a rejected line once and then ends the conversation rather than showing junk.

janhollow/narrator.py — the day's event, chosen from the seeded events/ templates by weight and by whether the station can host it (an event needing a dock cannot fire on a station without one), written up from what the crew actually did; and the time-skip paragraph that session 1 left as a placeholder.

janhollow/director.py — the one thread that calls Jan, with a priority order (a waiting time-skip first, then a new day, then a conversation), the chatter interval from the setting, and exponential backoff from 5 s to 2 minutes when Jan is not there.

sim.py — crew now carry what they are saying, their memories and their own drifting relationships; conversations are recorded, both sides remember them, and talking to someone warms them to you by one, capped at three. A new station day raises a flag the director picks up, so nothing slow ever runs on the tick.
'Off' is now a chatter level like any other, because the levels are a registry.

static/ — speech bubbles that wrap and are drawn in a pass above every sprite, the log styled by kind (spoken lines, the narrator's story, movements dimmed), and a Voices panel with live counts, what the director is doing, and a button each for a conversation and for the narrator.
verified: tests: 49 pass (19 from session 1, 30 new). The 30 run with Jan switched off: the guard's rules each pinned by the real bad sample that made them exist, the client's thinking flag and its one-at-a-time lane (four threads, maximum overlap of one), the role preference, pair selection, a conversation applied to the world, a rejected line retried then dropped, Jan being down staying quiet, the chatter interval including off, the away mode forbidding models, the director's priority order, and backoff.

Live, through the real models: conversations in the mess hall on the 0.8B, and the narrator on the 4B producing 'Morning Hum on Janhollow — The crew gathers for breakfast, enjoying Bo's fresh fruit and coffee while Cobalt brews to settle the lingering dust...' which wove the crew's ACTUAL conversations together with the quiet-fault event template.
Live away-mode gate: with idle_closed set and no page heartbeat for 13 s, /api/world/voices reported allowed_now false and the director idle; one heartbeat later it was true again.

Screenshots looked at: two speech bubbles over the right crew with the speakers' name labels suppressed; the log showing crew lines, the narrator's story in its own block and movement lines dimmed; the settings pane showing the Off level and the live voices readout.
black and pyright clean on every file touched.
got_wrong_and_fixed: The app asked forge_jan for a model, got nothing, and silently used whatever Jan listed first — an unrelated 2B. Fixed by roles.py; found only because the live output was worse than the probe's.

A reply cut off at the token limit never closes its JSON, so raw {"line": "... went into a speech bubble. The guard now salvages the value from unterminated JSON, and rejects any scaffolding that still gets through.

The 0.8B parroted the previous line back three times running ('I'll check Vessa...'). The exact-match echo rule never fired because it never repeats verbatim, it repeats the shape. Added the parrot rule: a shared four-word run, or the same three opening words.
Conversations degraded at the fourth turn, so they are now two or three.

Lines rambled well past the eighteen words asked for, including first-person prose ('A small smile tugged at the corners of my mouth...'). The hard cap is twenty words and the retry after a rejection is usually speech.
A bubble drawn inline in the sorted pass was painted over by anyone standing south of the speaker. Bubbles are their own pass now.
Killed my own shell twice with pgrep -f, whose pattern matched the command line that contained it. Saved PIDs instead.
not_done_yet: No player: you still cannot walk in or type at anyone. That is session 4, and it needs no model work.
Memories are only the last thing someone said to you plus the day's story; nothing summarises them yet.
The narrator never transfers crew off the station or brings new ones in, which Emerson allowed.
Props still do not block movement.
what_the_quality_is_actually_like: Honest assessment: the 0.8B produces short, in-character, station-appropriate lines that are sometimes slightly odd ('You think like a lady, Vessa, don't you?'). It is coherent and never garbage now — no other languages, no narration, no JSON, no parroting, no third-person self-reference — but it is a 416 MB model and it reads like one. The 4B narrator is genuinely good. If the chatter is not good enough, the cheapest lever is the model: roles.py is one edit, and Jan already has a 2B, a 4B and a 9B.
notes_for_the_next_session: Rejected lines are written to ~/ForgeGameData/janhollow/rejected.jsonl, capped at 200. Read it before tuning a prompt — it is the record of how this model actually fails.
Never call Jan from the tick thread or a request handler; the director is the only caller and everything it does is on its own thread.
guard.judge is pure and cheap. Reuse it for anything a model says to the player in session 4 rather than writing a second set of rules.
